claims.text: A threshold level of lattice distortion caused by atomic-size mismatch promotes edge-dislocation super-jog formation in BCC high-entropy alloys.
Edge-dislocation super-jogs impede dislocation motion through temperature-insensitive barriers.
Super-jog-mediated impediment of dislocation motion causes a high-temperature strength plateau.
NbTaTiZrV0.5 is a BCC high-entropy alloy suitable as the baseline system.
The baseline NbTaTiZrV0.5 alloy has moderate atomic-size mismatch.
The baseline alloy has a typical dislocation network.
Substitution with oversized or undersized atoms can controllably increase or decrease atomic-size mismatch and lattice distortion.
NbTaTiZrV0.5 exhibits approximately temperature-independent strength over 673–1073 K, including a more clearly identified platform over 873–1073 K.
Local lattice distortion alters dislocation-core configurations.
Greater local lattice distortion promotes edge-dislocation super-jog formation.
Low-distortion HEAs predominantly deform through screw-dislocation-mediated plasticity.
Screw-dislocation-controlled plasticity shows thermally activated softening with increasing temperature.
Higher-distortion alloys will retain yield strength and display a plateau over 673–1073 K.
Lower-distortion control alloys will show decreasing yield strength with increasing temperature.
The moderate-distortion baseline follows conventional temperature-dependent dislocation behavior.
The proposed mechanism is limited to significantly distorted BCC HEAs and may not apply to FCC HEAs or alloys with minimal atomic-size mismatch.

contradictions.description: NbTaTiZrV0.5 is presented as the moderate-distortion baseline following conventional temperature-dependent behavior, but the stated conditions describe the relevant range as one where a strength plateau is observed; the cited same-system record specifically reports the plateau in NbTaTiZrV0.5.
